title: How do you handle hostility when you openly share that you use AI?
author: WalkingDadPG
selftext:
I’m making games alongside a full-time job and family life, and I document the process on my How to Make Games with AI channel. The tools, the mistakes, the fixes, and the decisions I still have to make.

Recently, I received comments ranging from “The smartest video I've seen in a longtime.” to “oh my bad i almost liked and then saw you used ai! bye!” And then there was “death to ai.”

The “almost liked” comment is the one I keep thinking about. Apparently something appealed to them until they learned how it was made.

I understand that people have objections to AI, including concerns about training data and its impact on artists. I’m willing to discuss those. But comments like these don’t give me much to respond to or learn from.

Since people here are actually using these tools: have you had useful conversations with someone who initially reacted this way? What helped? Or do you usually leave it alone and keep sharing your work?

I want to stay open about my process. I’d also like to understand the criticism without every post becoming the same argument.

The attached video shows how I work on Fallen Nights and my other game projects: asking for changes I can test, reworking generated art that doesn’t fit, and changing design decisions after playtesting. It also includes a section on AI criticism and responsibility. Curious how others here are navigating this.
